title: How do we write four fractions in descending order?
description: Two lists of four fractions are each written from the greatest to the least. The board gives the fractions of a list the same fractional unit, orders the top numbers, and checks by going back to the first fractions.
teaching_notes: One idea: once the fractions of a list share one bottom number, the order of the top numbers is the order of the fractions. Watch for students who write the list from the least when asked for the greatest first.

video_script.why: A learner orders fractions by the method of the solved example: find a common multiple of the bottom numbers, rewrite every fraction with it, and order the top numbers.
video_script.substitution: the book's own two lists of four fractions
video_script.anchor: two lists of four fractions written on the board
video_script.payoff_line: the order of the top numbers is the order of the fractions

final_answer.spoken: in the first list the order is thirteen fourths, twenty-five sixteenths, seven eighths, seventeen thirty-seconds, and in the second list it is twelve fifths, five fourths, three fourths, seven twelfths

video_script.fraction_reading: twenty-five sixteenths, seven eighths, thirteen fourths, seventeen thirty-seconds, three fourths, twelve fifths, seven twelfths, five fourths
never_show: the sorted order before the top numbers are compared
maths_rules: check: 104/32 divided top and bottom by 8 is 13/4; 144/60 divided top and bottom by 12 is 12/5
video_script.design: Two lists of four fractions stay on the board. Each list is rewritten with one bottom number, as in the solved examples. The top numbers are ordered from the greatest, and the check divides back to the first fractions.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two lists of fractions: 25/16, 7/8, 13/4, 17/32 and 3/4, 12/5, 7/12, 5/4; an arrow labelled greatest to least

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.lists: the two lists of four fractions appear with an arrow labelled greatest to least
marks.ask: a question mark appears above each list

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it has two lists of fractions.
<bookmark mark='lists'/>Each list must be written in descending order, which means from the greatest to the least.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we put four fractions in order?

beats.on_screen: the two lists hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: four fractions with different bottom numbers, then the same four with one bottom number; the top numbers are circled

marks.unit: four fractions with different bottom numbers sit in a row with a question mark
marks.order: the same four fractions appear with one bottom number and the top numbers are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>Fractions with different bottom numbers are hard to put in order.
<bookmark mark='order'/>When all of them have the same bottom number, the top numbers give the order.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Given, the first list is twenty-five sixteenths, seven eighths, thirteen fourths and seventeen thirty-seconds.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second list is three fourths, twelve fifths, seven twelfths and five fourths.

beats.on_screen: To find: each list in descending order
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each list in descending order.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: list 1: 16, 8 and 4 all go into 32; use 32

marks.way: the words find a common multiple of the bottom numbers are written
marks.thirtytwo: 16, 8, 4 and 32 are written and 32 is circled

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>Step one, we use the same way as the solved example in your book. Find a common multiple of the bottom numbers of the first list.
<bookmark mark='thirtytwo'/>Sixteen, eight and four all go into thirty-two, which is already a bottom number. Use thirty-two.

marks.second: 13/4 changes to 104/32 and 17/32 stays the same

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, multiply the top and the bottom of each fraction. Twenty-five sixteenths is fifty thirty-seconds, and seven eighths is twenty-eight thirty-seconds.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Thirteen fourths is one hundred and four thirty-seconds. Seventeen thirty-seconds stays the same.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: top numbers 104 > 50 > 28 > 17; list 1 from the greatest: 13/4, 25/16, 7/8, 17/32

marks.tops: the top numbers 104, 50, 28 and 17 are lined up from the greatest
marks.list: the first list is written in the new order

narration: <bookmark mark='tops'/>Step three, the top numbers, from the greatest, are one hundred and four, fifty, twenty-eight and seventeen.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The first list is thirteen fourths, twenty-five sixteenths, seven eighths, then seventeen thirty-seconds.

marks.sixty: 4, 5 and 12 are written and 60 is circled

beats.colours: the common bottom number = accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='sixty'/>Step four, in the second list, four, five and twelve all go into sixty.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Three fourths is forty-five sixtieths. Twelve fifths is one hundred and forty-four sixtieths.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Seven twelfths is thirty-five sixtieths. Five fourths is seventy-five sixtieths.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: top numbers 144 > 75 > 45 > 35; list 2 from the greatest: 12/5, 5/4, 3/4, 7/12

marks.tops: the top numbers 144, 75, 45 and 35 are lined up from the greatest
marks.list: the second list is written in the new order

narration: <bookmark mark='tops'/>Step five, the top numbers, from the greatest, are one hundred and forty-four, seventy-five, forty-five and thirty-five.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The second list is twelve fifths, five fourths, three fourths, then seven twelfths.

beats.on_screen: Check: 104/32 divided top and bottom by 8 is 13/4; 144/60 divided top and bottom by 12 is 12/5

marks.back: 104/32 is divided top and bottom by 8 and 13/4 comes back
marks.back2: 144/60 is divided top and bottom by 12 and 12/5 comes back

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step six, check by going back. One hundred and four thirty-seconds divided by eight, top and bottom, is thirteen fourths again.
<bookmark mark='back2'/>One hundred and forty-four sixtieths divided by twelve, top and bottom, is twelve fifths again.

marks.ans: the two lists are written in order and boxed
marks.great: the greatest and the least of each list are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>With one fractional unit, the order of the top numbers is the order of the fractions.

<bookmark mark='great'/>In the first list, the greatest is thirteen fourths and the least is seventeen thirty-seconds. <bookmark mark='great2'/>In the second list, the greatest is twelve fifths and the least is seven twelfths.
